styles.name: Toy Press
styles.coreTrick: Every pressable control sits on a hard, zero-blur lip in a darker shade of its own face and drops by that depth when pressed, with cards as flat bordered trays.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary becomes the main key face and its lip is the same hue shaded 9-24 L darker; secondary/accent are tints and the small art; light mode keeps the brand canvas, dark mode derives a deep canvas from the primary hue. A pale or near-black primary gets a 2px lip-shade edge and the headline word flips to ink on a marker strip; a muted primary is used as-is (no recolour).

styles.name: Transit Wayfinding
styles.coreTrick: Every message sits on a fixed black sign panel while each client colour is rationed to a route (a line stroke plus a lettered bullet) and one fixed yellow means alert.
styles.colourRecipe: Canvas is fixed (#16181A / #E8E8E4); each of primary, secondary, accent is tinted until it holds 3:1 on black (and shaded for the white map paper in light mode) and used only as a route; primary also fills the main action. A muted or grey brand still tints to 3:1 but the routes then look similar (no recolour).

remainder.whyCode: Many per-component overrides keeping signs black in a light page

styles.notes: Strongly rule-based; the semantic colour mapping (colour = route) is a framework-level idea, not a CSS trick.

styles.name: WPA Screenprint
styles.coreTrick: The three brand colours are muted into flat print inks on fixed cream paper, with a hard 2px second-ink offset block under actions and multiplied overprint where inks cross.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary, secondary and accent are muted (S<=40, L 42-60) into spot inks; the primary is then moved by lightness until the label (cream on light, forest on dark) holds 4.7:1; canvas is fixed cream or forest night. A neon brand prints as a dull ink; a muted brand passes almost unchanged.

remainder.what: Offset block clearing rules per kit component
remainder.whyCode: Individual kit shapes (split buttons, fab) with bespoke radius and offset

styles.name: Xerox Punk
styles.coreTrick: A fixed dark wall of pasted scraps where every element looks hand-made: seeded ransom-note tiles, filter-torn paper, tape, marker circles, with the primary snapped to one of five Day-Glo inks.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary snaps by hue to one of five Day-Glo inks (grey takes yellow, blues and violets take pink) and is used as the single fluoro; secondary is held back, accent is one headline tile; canvas fixed near-black or newsprint; app screens switch back to the true brand primary.

remainder.what: Seeded ransom headline with per-letter face, ground, size, tilt, scissor clip, photo tiles
remainder.whyCode: Per-letter randomised layout with font pool, load triggers and grouping rules

remainder.what: Procedural one-bit halftone photograph
remainder.whyCode: Raster-like figure generated from math

remainder.what: Wall collage and photo card art
remainder.whyCode: Hand-positioned remnants and torn SVG filter defs

remainder.what: Hand-drawn marker circle, strike and staple paths
remainder.whyCode: Authored path data

remainder.what: Kit signature with 120 lines of hand-made component rules
remainder.whyCode: Per-component shapes (zig-zag cut lines, hatch checkbox, hazard edge) bespoke by design

styles.notes: Most of the identity is code (random layout and torn filters). A move library would cover colour, offsets, stamps and sheets, not the ransom headline. Two near-duplicate kit blocks (classic and v2) in the css; lines cited are the live v2.

styles.name: Xerox
styles.coreTrick: Everything is toner (#111) on one pale paper stock, with SVG alpha-threshold and displacement filters that degrade shapes like successive photocopy generations.
styles.colourRecipe: The primary only picks the paper: its hue bucket chooses one pale stock (canary, salmon, pink, lilac, blue, green) for the whole canvas, and appears as ink only in one multiplied stamp; secondary and accent are never printed but copied as dot density in the palette. A grey primary gives white stock.

remainder.what: States hook renders initial through three generation filters
remainder.whyCode: Custom markup

remainder.what: html2canvas export workarounds
remainder.whyCode: Filters and gradient dots not supported by export

styles.notes: Filters are the whole point and are not exportSafe. Stock chooser is data (hue buckets) and well within a move.

notes: Schema fit: ok. Gaps: (1) contrast-fit and similar colour searches are framework helpers, not styles; classed needs-code but one shared function serves all styles. (2) "variant" params hold enums that switch shapes (switch, slider, progress); a generator needs a template per enum value. (3) Seeded randomness (xerox-punk) has no schema slot. (4) Kit line ranges point at the live signature block; xerox-punk and xerox keep a duplicate "classic" block that was ignored.
